purpose: Recommended reversible sample-ID and metadata convention for user-supplied experimental data. It is a compatibility convention, not a requirement to rename established cohorts.

segments.description: Unique biological sample or library identifier; zero-pad numbers when practical.
Biological replicate within the experimental group. Technical replicates must use a separate `Tech` field and are not independent samples.
Treatment, condition, genotype group, or environment; use `TrtControl`, `TrtDrought`, or similarly explicit labels.
Time point; use `Ti00`, `Ti06h`, `Ti7d`, or another unit-explicit value.
Library-preparation, lane, or sequencing batch, for example `B01`.

rules: Use underscores only to separate labelled segments; do not use a bare `T` because it is ambiguous between treatment and time.
For new synthetic or small studies, use `S###_R##_Trt<level>_Ti<time>_B##` and omit segments that do not apply.
For established cohorts, preserve original IDs and provide a sample-metadata table mapping them to the canonical fields instead of renaming files.
Count-matrix column names, alignment sample names, and metadata `sample_id` values must match exactly.
A metadata table is authoritative; sample IDs are a convenience and must not be the only record of design variables.
